criteria.name: Functionality
criteria.description: All required functions work correctly (sum, average, min, max, filter)

levels.label: Complete
levels.description: All 5 functions work correctly with various inputs including edge cases (empty arrays, negative numbers)

criteria.name: Modern JavaScript
criteria.description: Uses ES6+ features appropriately (arrow functions, const/let, array methods)

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Excellent use of arrow functions, const/let, reduce, filter, map, spread operator where appropriate

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Good use of modern features with minor missed opportunities

levels.label: Acceptable
levels.description: Some modern features used but relies heavily on traditional loops

levels.label: Outdated
levels.description: Uses var, traditional for loops only, no modern array methods

levels.label: Missing
levels.description: Code does not run or uses incorrect syntax

criteria.name: Error Handling
criteria.description: Handles edge cases and invalid input gracefully

levels.label: Complete
levels.description: Handles empty arrays, non-array inputs, and invalid values; provides meaningful error messages or default values

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Handles most edge cases but misses some scenarios

levels.label: Minimal
levels.description: Basic error handling only (e.g., checks for empty array)

levels.label: Missing
levels.description: No error handling; crashes on edge cases

criteria.name: Code Quality
criteria.description: Clean, readable code with good naming and structure

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Descriptive function/variable names, consistent formatting, JSDoc comments

levels.label: Good
levels.description: Good names and formatting with minor issues

levels.label: Acceptable
levels.description: Functional but poor naming or inconsistent style

levels.label: Poor
levels.description: Hard to read, single-letter variables, no formatting
